**Routing report from the `domain:metadata` lane — ⛔ not claiming, ⛔ no label changed.**

PM session `session_01XeQRiAa7vYRVX5Fog7Zby8`.

The file this card corrects is **`content/docs/api/metadata-api.mdx`** (confirmed present at that path on `origin/main`). The lane table routes `content/docs/**` to **`domain:devx`**, so by the anchoring rule this is a devx card whose *subject* happens to be the metadata API — the classic case the rule exists to disambiguate, since the label follows the package the fix lands in and never the issue's title vocabulary.

⇒ Suggested disposition (triage's call): relabel `domain:devx` (#6023's lane). No opinion offered on its content or priority.

**Scope update: this card gains a third refusal class, from #8421 / PR #8770 (in review, not yet landed).**

This card's premise is that `metadata-api.mdx` documents `PUT /meta/:type/:name` as *"Create or update a metadata item"* without saying some types refuse creates — *"now two of them"*.

PR #8770 adds a **third and differently-shaped** class: a type **name the platform does not have** is now refused outright. `PUT /api/v1/meta/fieldz/showcase_task.title` changes from `200 {"success":true}` to `400 INVALID_REQUEST`, persisting nothing.

It differs from the two already on this card in a way the doc line will need to reflect:

- the existing two are **per-type** refusals — a recognised type that declines creates;
- this one refuses because the **type name is not recognised at all**, so it is a statement about the whole `:type` path parameter rather than about any particular type.

Line 26 of that page is the one most affected — it currently explains only the singular/plural folding (*"`object` and `objects` address the same type"*) and says nothing about what happens to a name that folds to nothing.

⚠️ **Verify against `origin/main` when this card is taken**: PR #8770 is under review and deliberately **not** auto-merged pending a maintainer ratification of two narrowings, so the third class is not live yet. Do not document it until it lands.

Also worth knowing for whoever takes this: PR #8770 refuses on the **mint** verb only. Reads and delete stay open, measured and argued in that PR — so the doc line belongs on `PUT`, not on the page's general description of `/meta`.

### Related: the docs-drift gate did not flag this page

PR #8770 changes `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/spec`; the drift check listed **106** hand-written pages by package dependency and `content/docs/api/metadata-api.mdx` was **not among them** — the one page that documents the endpoint whose accept set the PR narrows. Filed separately so the gate gap has its own card rather than living in this one's comments.

**Suspected `domain:*` mislabel — reported, ⛔ not corrected.** From the `domain:metadata` execution seat (#6367), PM session `session_01NTKPDRoynY8i3HmdSFUxFj`. An execution seat ⛔ does not change `domain:*` — that field has a single producer (triage) — so this is a report, and the card was skipped rather than dispatched this round.

**Why I think it is misrouted.** The anchoring rule sets the domain by *the package the fix lands in*, and this card's fix lands entirely in documentation prose:

- the named defect is `content/docs/api/metadata-api.mdx:49`;
- the suggested fix is one caveat sentence on that entry;
- the card's "explicitly NOT in scope" section rules out the only non-docs surfaces it touches (the refusal messages themselves, and `releases/v17.mdx`).

`content/docs/**` routes to **`domain:devx`** (#6023) by the lane table. Nothing in the deliverable lands in `packages/metadata*` or `packages/platform-objects`, which is this seat's scope.

**Not a mechanical relabel — one judgement call for triage.** The card's subject is a *metadata contract* (`allowRuntimeCreate` per-type gating, and which types refuse creates), so the "domain of the subject" and the "domain of the landing site" genuinely diverge here. The anchoring rule is explicit that the landing site wins and that title vocabulary must not decide it — which points at `devx` — but this is triage's call, not mine, and I would rather flag the divergence than quietly route around it.

**Prerequisite worth flagging either way, whoever takes it.** The card says ⛔ *do not enumerate `field` and `job` by name unless the enumeration is generated* — because a hand-written list of retired types is the exact staleness shape that created this card. Whoever implements it should first check whether a generated readable surface for the per-type `allowRuntimeCreate` flags actually exists; if it does not, the "point at wherever the flags are readable" instruction has no target, and that is a scope question to settle **before** dispatch rather than during it.

⛔ Labels untouched (`documentation`, `pm:queue`, `domain:metadata` left exactly as they stand); ⛔ no assignee set. The card remains dispatchable for whichever lane owns it.

Claiming for dispatch, at the maintainer's prompting.

## First, correcting my own earlier handling of this card

On 2026-08-16 (`5305713030`) this seat reported a suspected `domain:*` mislabel and **skipped the card**. The report was right; the skip was wrong. ⛔ An execution seat does not change `domain:*` — but the label as it stands says `domain:metadata`, which **is** this seat's lane, and the `devx` seat cannot see a card labelled for mine. Skipping it on the strength of a suggestion triage has not acted on left it stranded in the one state where nobody picks it up. Dispatching it under the label it actually carries; if triage relabels mid-flight, the work moves with it.

## 裁决 — not re-litigable

1. ⛔ **Do NOT hand-enumerate the refusing types.** A hand-written list of retired types is the exact staleness shape that created this card. The caveat sentence points at wherever the per-type flags are readable; it does not restate them. This is the same defect class as #9190 (`REFERENCE_PATHS` hand-curated) and #8990's census (a hand-written figure measured 12 where there were 57) — do not add a ninth instance to that tally.

2. **The scope prerequisite is a MEASUREMENT and it comes first.** Determine whether a **generated** readable surface for the per-type `allowRuntimeCreate` / `allowOrgOverride` flags actually exists. ⚠️ If it does not, the "point at wherever the flags are readable" instruction has no target — **stop and report**. That is a scope question to settle before writing, not during. ⛔ Do not invent a surface to point at.

3. **Three refusal classes, and they are not the same shape.** Two are **per-type** (a recognised type that declines creates). The third, from #8421 / PR #8770, refuses because the **type name is not recognised at all** — a statement about the whole `:type` path parameter, not about any type. ⚠️ Measure whether PR #8770 has landed on `origin/main` before documenting the third; on 2026-08-14 it was explicitly *"not live yet — do not document until it lands."* If it is still unlanded, document two and say so.

4. **The third class belongs on `PUT` only.** PR #8770 refuses on the **mint** verb; reads and delete stay open, measured and argued in that PR. ⛔ Do not attach it to the page's general description of `/meta`.

5. ⛔ **Never edit `content/docs/releases/`.** The card's own "explicitly NOT in scope" section already rules out `releases/v17.mdx` and the refusal messages themselves. Both stay out.

## PM 机制假设 — measure, don't inherit

- The file is `content/docs/api/metadata-api.mdx`, the defect at **line 49**, and **line 26** (which currently explains only singular/plural folding and says nothing about a name that folds to nothing) is the one most affected by the third class. All three line numbers are from August comments — **re-derive them**, the file has almost certainly moved.
- ⚠️ **The `/meta` singular/plural story is changing under this card.** #9180 is a live maintainer ruling that the type segment is ALWAYS singular, and its step ① landed (#9157 / PR #9191). Line 26's folding prose may now be describing a tolerance that is being retired. **Check #9180's state before writing anything about folding**, and if the prose you'd write would contradict that ruling, ⛔ stop and report rather than documenting a tolerance on its way out.
- The docs-drift gate did **not** flag this page for PR #8770 (it listed 106 pages by package dependency and missed the one page documenting the endpoint whose accept set the PR narrowed). So there is no tooling backstop here — the artifact is the evidence.

## Model tier

Clause ② judged **not triggered**: documentation prose only; the fix lands entirely in `content/docs/**`; no accept/reject behaviour changes, no `packages/spec/**`, no error-code ledger, no `*.zod.ts`. Dispatching at `sonnet`. ⚠️ Fence: if closing this requires touching a refusal's message or its status, **stop and report** — that is a different card and a different tier.

## Route

Worktree-first. Changeset per repo rules. Draft PR. ⛔ Never merge your own PR.

## Measurements that determined scope

**1. Generated readable surface for the per-type flags -- exists, partially.** `content/docs/references/kernel/metadata-plugin.mdx` is auto-generated (`build-docs.ts`; header says "AUTO-GENERATED -- DO NOT EDIT") and documents `MetadataTypeRegistryEntry.allowRuntimeCreate` / `allowOrgOverride` (existence, type, default) sourced from `packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts`. It does **not** enumerate the registry's concrete per-type values -- `build-docs.ts` documents the Zod schema, not the `DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY` array's contents. A separate, **pre-existing, hand-written** table with concrete current values already lives at `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx#overlay-whitelist-shared-db-tenancy-invariant` (added under #7893, not created or touched by this PR). Since both targets already existed and neither had to be invented, I did not stop -- the caveat links both instead of hand-enumerating `field`/`job` inline in `metadata-api.mdx` itself.

**2. PR #8770 (#8421) landed status -- PM's caution was stale, corrected by measurement.** The comment on this card said "as of 2026-08-14 ... not live yet -- do not document until it lands." Checked `mcp__github__pull_request_read`: `merged: true`, `merged_at: 2026-08-15T11:10:35Z`, merge commit reachable from `origin/main`. It has been live for two days. Documented accordingly.

**3. `unrecognisedMetaTypeRefusal` vs. the already-documented `metaUrlSpellingRefusal` -- two different predicates, confirmed by reading `packages/spec/src/shared/metadata-url-spelling.ts`.** `main` already carries a caveat (lines 14-17 of the file, landed 2026-08-17 by PR #9245 closing #9193) for `metaUrlSpellingRefusal` -- a misspelling of a *declared* type (`viewes` for `view`), which fires on nine verbs including reads. That is **not** the refusal this card is about. #8421/PR #8770's `unrecognisedMetaTypeRefusal` refuses a segment that is not a metadata type at all (`fieldz`), and is consumed only by `refuseUnmintableMetaType`, whose sole call site I confirmed is inside `saveMetaItem` -- the `PUT` path. So it belongs on `PUT` only, matching the card's mandate, and is a genuinely separate gap from what #9245 already closed.

**4. #9180 (singular/plural ruling) -- read in full; its step (1) (#9157/PR #9191) has landed, its step (3) has not.** Step (1) narrows three *read* verbs (`historyMetaItem`/`auditMetaItem`/`findReferencesToMeta`) to refuse plurals. Step (3), which would rewrite `metadata-api.mdx`'s "singular or plural" folding prose, is still "to file." That prose (currently around line 30-37, moved from the August-comment line 26) remains an accurate description of the currently-landed behavior for `GET /meta/:type` and `GET /meta/:type/:name`, so it was left untouched -- writing "types are singular" now would document a tolerance ahead of the ruling that retires it.

## Final prose added (the artifact, quoted per dispatch instructions)

Under `### PUT /meta/:type/:name`:

> Creates are gated per type: `MetadataTypeRegistryEntry.allowRuntimeCreate` decides whether a **brand-new** name may be minted under that type at all, separately from whether an item that already exists may be overlaid (`allowOrgOverride`). A type that declines the create half still accepts updates to names that already exist, and its refusal -- `403 NOT_CREATABLE` -- names the route that does work. The flags are documented on [`MetadataTypeRegistryEntry`](/docs/references/kernel/metadata-plugin#metadatatyperegistryentry); which types currently decline which half is tracked in the [overlay whitelist](/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle#overlay-whitelist-shared-db-tenancy-invariant) rather than enumerated on this page, so this caveat doesn't go stale the next time a type is retired.
>
> This verb also refuses a `:type` segment that is not a metadata type the platform declares at all -- not a recognised spelling, and not a misspelling of one either -- with `400 INVALID_REQUEST`, before any namespace is minted for it. The refusal is scoped to this verb: `GET` and `DELETE` on an item that already exists are unaffected. See [unrecognised type spelling](/docs/api/error-catalog#invalid_request--unrecognised-type-spelling) in the error catalog for the envelope -- the same code and status cover both this refusal and the misspelling one above; the message text tells them apart.

## Scope respected

- `content/docs/releases/**` untouched.
- The refusal messages/codes/statuses themselves untouched (tier fence held -- no `packages/spec` or runtime source touched, docs only).
- No new `error-catalog.mdx` entry added -- the existing "Not this error" callout under the misspelling entry already states the second refusal's envelope shape and is what the new caveat links to; a full dedicated entry would be a separate, larger change.
- No changeset: `content/docs/**` maps to no npm package (same treatment as precedent PR #9245). `skip-changeset` label applied and read back: PR #9289 carries `["size/s", "skip-changeset"]`.

## One platform-behavior note, not an action item

Reading the PR back after creation, its body's attribution footer came back as `_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01NTKPDRoynY8i3HmdSFUxFj)_` -- a different session ID (the PM's) than the one I wrote. Per AGENTS.md this is documented platform rewrite behavior and evidence of nothing else; not corrected, just noting it for the record.
